questions.question: Gandhi Jayanti marks the birthday of the father of the nation Mahatma Gandhi, who was born at __________.
questions.solution: Mahatma Gandhi, the Father of the Nation, was born on October 2, 1869, at Porbandar, a coastal town in Gujarat. His birthplace is now preserved as a memorial called Kirti Mandir.

questions.question: Muharram is the ____________ month of the Islamic Calendar and is considered a holy month.
questions.solution: Muharram is the first month of the Islamic calendar. It is one of the four sacred months of the year and holds deep religious significance, particularly the tenth day known as Ashura.

questions.question: With which of the following communities is the word 'Langar' (community kitchen) mainly associated?
questions.solution: The concept of Langar (community kitchen) is a central feature of Sikhism. It was established by Guru Nanak Dev Ji to uphold the principle of equality, where everyone—regardless of religion, caste, or background—sits together on the floor to share a free vegetarian meal.

questions.question: Sakewa is a religious festival celebrated by the Kirat Khambu Rai community of ________.
questions.solution: Sakewa is a nine-day nature-worship festival celebrated by the Kirat Khambu Rai community of Sikkim. It involves the Sili dance and prayers offered to the Earth (Mother Nature) for a good harvest and protection from calamities.

questions.question: ‘Hampi Utsava,’ which is celebrated in Karnataka, is also called ____________. The festival that captures the pomp, splendour and glory of the historical period of Karnataka is celebrated over a week.
questions.solution: The 'Hampi Utsava' in Karnataka is popularly known as Vijaya Utsava. It commemorates the glory of the ancient Vijayanagara Empire and is held amidst the ruins of Hampi, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

questions.question: The Indian festival of Holi comes every year in the season of:
questions.solution: The festival of Holi, the festival of colors, is celebrated in India during the spring season. It falls on the Purnima (full moon) of the Hindu month of Phalguna, marking the end of winter and the arrival of bloom.

questions.question: Mewar festival is celebrated during the _______ festival at Udaipur
questions.solution: The Mewar Festival in Udaipur is celebrated to coincide with the Gangaur festival. It marks the transition to spring and involves a grand procession where images of Gauri (Parvati) are taken to Lake Pichola.

questions.question: In which country is the ‘Kachin Manaw Festival’ celebrated?
questions.solution: The Kachin Manaw Festival is one of the most famous and important festivals in Myanmar (Burma). It is a celebration of the Kachin people to mark the New Year, victory in battle, and the reunion of tribes.

questions.question: _________ is a significant festival of the Parsi people who practice Zoroastrianism as it marks the birth anniversary of Zoroaster.
questions.solution: Khordad Sal marks the birth anniversary of Zoroaster (Prophet Spitaman Zarathustra), the founder of Zoroastrianism. It is a day of great rejoicing for the Parsi community, falling on the sixth day of the month of Farvardin.

questions.question: Which of the following is the festival of Kerala that heralds the harvest season, lasts for 10 days, and has snake boat races etc?
questions.solution: Onam is the premier harvest festival of Kerala, lasting for 10 days. It is famous for the Vallam Kali (snake boat races), Pookalam (flower carpets), and the legend of the benevolent King Mahabali.

questions.question: Bali Yatra, is a traditional cultural festival of which state?
questions.solution: Bali Yatra (Voyage to Bali) is a massive open-air fair held in Cuttack, Odisha. It commemorates the ancient maritime history of Odia seafarers (Sadhabas) who sailed to distant lands like Bali, Java, and Sumatra for trade.

questions.question: Jamshedi Navroz is a festival of _________ community.
questions.solution: Jamshedi Navroz is the celebration of the Persian New Year by the Parsi community. Named after the legendary Persian King Jamshed, it occurs on the Spring Equinox (usually March 21st).

questions.question: Good Friday is related to:
questions.solution: Good Friday is a solemn day in Christianity that commemorates the crucifixion of Jesus Christ and his death at Calvary. It is observed during Holy Week as a time of reflection and penance.

questions.question: _________ is a form of Sikh festival.
questions.solution: Hola Mohalla is a Sikh festival started by Guru Gobind Singh Ji. It usually falls a day after Holi and is a time for Sikhs to demonstrate their martial skills, including mock battles and Gatka (traditional martial arts).

questions.question: What is the name of the festival that ends the Holy Ramzan month?
questions.solution: Eid-Ul-Fitr is the festival of 'Breaking the Fast' that marks the end of the holy month of Ramzan. It is a day of gratitude, charity (Zakat-al-Fitr), and community feasting.

questions.question: Hemis festival is associated with which of the following religions?
questions.solution: The Hemis Festival is a famous Buddhist festival celebrated at the Hemis Monastery in Ladakh. It commemorates the birth anniversary of Guru Padmasambhava and features the iconic masked Cham dances.

questions.question: Dussehra festival is celebrated in which of the following Hindu months?
questions.solution: The Dussehra festival (Vijayadashami) is celebrated in the Hindu month of Ashwin. It marks the victory of Lord Rama over Ravana and Goddess Durga over the buffalo demon Mahishasura.

questions.question: The Braj festival in ________ is held every year for two days in the Shukla Paksha of the Phalgun month, a few days before Holi.
questions.solution: The Braj Festival is a vibrant celebration held in the Bharatpur district of Rajasthan. It takes place just before Holi in the month of Phalgun and is dedicated to the eternal love of Lord Krishna and Radha.

questions.question: Pinjore heritage festival is organised by the state of ________.
questions.solution: The Pinjore Heritage Festival is organized annually by the Haryana Tourism Department at the 17th-century Yadavindra Gardens (Pinjore Gardens) to showcase the state's rich cultural and architectural heritage.

questions.question: In Gujarat, the festival Makar Sankranti is celebrated as:
questions.solution: In Gujarat, Makar Sankranti is celebrated as Uttarayan. It marks the day the sun begins its northward journey and is famous worldwide for its International Kite Festival.

questions.question: Which state organises the Lokrang Festival?
questions.solution: The Lokrang Festival is a prominent five-day folk festival organized by the Madhya Pradesh Adivasi Lok Kala Academy in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. It starts on Republic Day (January 26th) and showcases tribal and folk traditions.

questions.question: The Kutch festival is held at ___________.
questions.solution: The famous Rann Utsav or Kutch Festival is centered around Bhuj and the 'Tent City' at Dhordo in Gujarat. It celebrates the unique landscape of the White Rann (salt desert) under the moonlight.

questions.question: Doljatra is a festival of which state from followings?
questions.solution: Doljatra (or Doul Utsav) is the regional version of Holi celebrated in Assam and West Bengal. In Assam, it is particularly famous at the Satras (monasteries) like Barpeta, where it is dedicated to Lord Krishna.

questions.question: Easter is a religious festival of:
questions.solution: Easter is a major religious festival for Christians, celebrating the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, which occurred three days after his crucifixion on Good Friday.

questions.question: Manipur's ____________ tribe celebrates the ‘Gaan-Ngai’ festival, which is a post-harvest festival of the tribe living in the regions of Manipur.
questions.solution: The Gaan-Ngai festival is a grand post-harvest celebration of the Zeliangrong community (comprising Zeme, Liangmai, and Rongmei tribes) in Manipur. It is a time for thanksgiving and honoring ancestors.

questions.question: Which of the following date is observed as a national festival?
questions.solution: 2 October is observed as a National Festival in India (Gandhi Jayanti). Along with Republic Day (January 26) and Independence Day (August 15), it is one of the three official national holidays.

questions.question: Which of the following states is famous for celebrating the festival of Vijaya Dashmi, which marks the end of Durga Puja?
questions.solution: While celebrated across India, West Bengal is world-renowned for its Durga Puja, which concludes with Vijaya Dashami (Sindoor Khela and immersion of the idols), symbolizing the victory of good over evil.

questions.question: ‘Tamu Lochar’ is one of the traditional festivals of the ____________ of Sikkim. It is celebrated to mark the beginning of their new year, which falls on the 15th day of Pusa, according to the Hindu calendar Vikram Samvat and 30th December in the English calendar.
questions.solution: Tamu Lochar is the traditional New Year festival of the Gurung community in Sikkim. It marks the change in the cycle of the zodiac and is celebrated with traditional dances, family gatherings, and community feasts.

questions.question: International Kite Festival is a popular cultural festival of which state?
questions.solution: The International Kite Festival (Uttarayan) is a hallmark cultural event of Gujarat. Thousands of people gather on rooftops to fly kites, and professional kite flyers from across the world visit Ahmedabad to participate.

questions.question: Which Indian festival is a festival of lights?
questions.solution: Diwali (Deepavali) is the quintessential Indian festival of lights. It involves lighting diyas, candles, and lamps to celebrate the return of Lord Rama to Ayodhya and the victory of light over darkness.

questions.question:
With reference to Chethiagiri Vihar festival consider the following statements and select the correct option.

i)It is a Buddhist festival.

ii) It is held at Sanchi, Madhya Pradesh.

iii) Relics of SariPutta and Maha Moggallana are worshiped.
questions.solution: All three statements about the Chethiagiri Vihar Festival are correct. It is a major Buddhist event in Sanchi (MP) where the sacred relics of Sari Putta and Maha Moggallana (chief disciples of Buddha) are brought out for public viewing.

questions.question: Every year in the month of February, this camel festival is organised by Rajasthan Tourism Development Corporation in __________.
questions.solution: The International Camel Festival is an annual event organized in Bikaner, Rajasthan. It features camel races, camel dances, and various cultural performances against the backdrop of the Junagarh Fort.

questions.question: Gurpurab is celebrated to commemorate the birthday of Guru Nank dev ji. He was the _________ guru of Sikhs?
questions.solution: Guru Nanak Dev Ji, whose birth is celebrated as Gurpurab (Guru Nanak Jayanti), was the first of the ten Sikh Gurus and the founder of Sikhism.

questions.question: The birthday of ________ is celebrated as the International Day of Non-Violence.
questions.solution: The birthday of Mahatma Gandhi (October 2) is observed worldwide as the International Day of Non-Violence, as established by the United Nations General Assembly to spread the message of peace and ahimsa.
